macroContext.narrative: Sweden's economy is in a moderately positive cycle. IMF projects 2.4% real GDP growth for 2026 (up from 1.8% in 2025). Fiscal position is sound: gross debt at ~31% GDP, near fiscal balance (net lending +0.5% GDP). Inflation is trending toward 2% target. These conditions mean both propositions (security detention and Skatteverket expansion) face no fiscal constraint — implementation cost is within budget.
macroContext.relevanceToMotions: Economic stability provides budgetary space for Migrationsverket detention expansion (prop. 2025/26:267) and Skatteverket IT investment (prop. 2025/26:261). Neither motion creates material fiscal risk. The primary implementation constraints are legal (ECHR, GDPR) rather than budgetary.
macroContext.skatteverketContext: Anti-fraud measures through expanded folkbokföring access are consistent with Sweden's high-trust administrative model. IMF has recognized Sweden's tax administration quality in Article IV consultations. Skatteverket expansion is fiscally efficient.
macroContext.securityContext: Swedish defense and security spending has been elevated since 2022 (NATO accession context). Security-threat migration detention is a marginal addition to existing security infrastructure costs.
